title: Ferdinand I to Johann Malvezzi, Augsburg, 23 January 1548 (DECODE R366)

steps.what: Fetched the eight R366 images and the record metadata from DECODE with a saved cookie.

Web searches for a published decipherment of the letter and for the Ferdinand-Malvezzi ciphers. No decipherment found; identified Austro-Turcica 1541-1552 as the edition that probably prints the letter, not freely available online.
Searched the DECODE record list around R366 and found the key records R367 (same shelfmark) and R386, with transcriptions DOC_R367 and DOC_R386.
Calibrated the sign values on p. 1 against the key images (sermone, tecum, quod, propter, tractatum, nobiscum, constituendae, autor).
Read the cipher runs page by page from zoomed crops, two subagents in parallel on pp. 1/4/7 and pp. 5/6. p. 4 read almost in full, pp. 5-6 read, pp. 1 and 7 read in part.

Looked for the letter in Austro-Turcica 1541-1552 via web search, the H-Net review and footnotes in Tracy, 'The Logic of Kleinkrieg' (AHY 2021) and Gürkan/Levantine Heritage papers. The edition is not online (no Google Books/HathiTrust full view found). Established only its neighbours: instructions for Malvezzi 24 Jan 1548 (reportedly no. 62), Ferdinand to Justus de Argento 13 Feb 1548 = no. 68, pp. 213-15. The 23 Jan letter's own number and text could not be seen, so the reading is neither confirmed nor corrected.

Checked the old 0.83 measure: a mark count over read_A/read_B (word counted read unless marked [?]); it did not test Latin sense and left out p. 1 cipher lines 1-8. Wrote reading_full.txt and measure_sense.py (shared 'la' model: word-form test plus 9-word window above the 2nd percentile of corpus windows; shuffled-letter control).
Re-transcribed from full-resolution crops all of p. 1's cipher (ll. 1-10), p. 4 l. 1, the sese/ulciscantur lines and the last line, p. 5 open words, p. 6 l. 14 and ll. 15-26, and all of p. 7.

Added the hand's variant sign values from the read pages: looped g-sign = d, stemmed circle with looped foot = q (before u) / r, footed Pi = g, P with small circle below = o, pointed cap = l. With them p. 7 and the p. 6 foot read straight through (magistrum horologiorum; de gentibus nostris in confiniis; captives freed by the Sultan).

Corrected 9 writer's slips forced by context (pacr->pacis, Turcrum, uiciscantur->ulciscantur, comutum->computum, factorum->facturum, expona->exponas, manutenea->manutenendam, faciam->faciamus, ordinaria). Left unread: the banker's surname after Gulielmo (signs give Semaslia, person not identified), one two-sign group before nominatione on p. 6, two lone v signs (probably uel).

measure_sense.py: p1 41/41, p4 114/114, p5 156/158, p6 134/136, p7 64/65; overall 509/514 = 0.990 (0.973 without the 9 slip-corrected words). Control with letters shuffled within words: 19/514 = 0.037 (code words only).

outcome.method_basis: The key is DECODE R367, a reconstruction filed at the same shelfmark (Military History Archive 1548/3), with a second copy R386; its sign values were calibrated on p. 1 and the cipher runs read from zoomed crops of R366.
outcome.notes: The substance is recovered in full: Ruestem Pasha's standing after the treaty; the French work to break the Habsburg-Ottoman peace because they dare not attack Charles V directly; Malvezzi's pay (2,800 + 1,500 ducats by Justus de Argento, a 3,000-ducat credit repayable at Venice); a master clockmaker to be brought by the secretary; what to answer about the frontier garrisons; and reciprocity for captives freed by the Sultan. Open: a banker's surname, one two-sign group, two lone v signs.

gaps.item: p. 5 l. 18, the banker's surname after Gulielmo
gaps.detail: every sign read (Semaslia); the person is not identified; Austro-Turcica 1541-1552 would name him

gaps.item: p. 6 l. 3, a two-sign group before nominatione
gaps.detail: e-sign + 8 fits no key value as written

gaps.item: p. 6 l. 24 and p. 7 l. 1, lone v signs between words
gaps.detail: v = f in the key; probably the clerk's mark for uel; not counted as read

outcome.fraction_read_source: measure_sense.py on reading_full.txt (5 Oct 2026): a plaintext word of the ciphered passages counts as read when it is marked read and, for non-code words, is a Latin word form under lang 'la' and its 9-word window scores above the 2nd percentile of corpus windows: 509/514 = 0.990 (p1 1.000, p4 1.000, p5 0.987, p6 0.985, p7 0.985); 0.973 without the 9 slip-corrected words. The earlier 0.83 was a [?]-mark count over read_A/read_B that omitted p. 1 ll. 1-8.

prior.where: No decipherment on DECODE or the web. Austro-Turcica 1541-1552 (Munich 1995) prints the Ferdinand-Malvezzi correspondence of early 1548 (Ferdinand's instructions for Malvezzi, 24 Jan 1548, reportedly no. 62; Ferdinand to Justus de Argento, Augsburg 13 Feb 1548, no. 68, pp. 213-15, per Tracy 2021), so this 23 Jan 1548 letter is probably printed there around nos. 62-67 (c. pp. 190-212); number unconfirmed, edition not online, not consulted (checked 2026-09-21).

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, and set the target with /goal. No target-specific intervention.
